Beállítom “The government made a mistake when it failed to build large reservoirs suitable for retaining water ten years ago", János Lázár stated last year, while serving as minister of construction and transportation in the Orbán government. As evidenced by a recently surfaced video, the former minister spoke about this during a December hearing before the Parliament’s Committees for Business Development and Sustainable Growth. His statement is in direct opposition to the narrative promoted by Fidesz (now an opposition party) in recent weeks, which claims that the Tisza government, which took office in May, is solely responsible for the country being unprepared for the historic drought and heatwave. At last December’s hearing, Lázár replied with blunt honesty to a point raised by László Lóránt Keresztes, then an independent member of Parliament and chairman of the committee, who criticized the government’s lack of a water management strategy. “You are absolutely right in saying that it is foolish to allow much more freshwater to leave the country than comes into it; this is simply untenable. […] ​​I’ll share a government secret with you: there’s a great deal of talk about this in government circles. […] There are currently 200 millimeters of water missing from the fields in the Great Plain.” “We’re heading toward total destruction. There are geographical and natural phenomena which give us cause for grave concern. Your figures are completely accurate; the water shortage is a brutal reality, and I can tell you that it hasn’t really been decided what we want to do,” Lázár acknowledged, admitting the mistake of the government at the time. When asked about János Lázár admission that the Orbán government had failed to adequately prepare the country for a severe water shortage, Fidesz’s parliamentary group leader, János Bóka said on Monday that the Tisza government alone is responsible for the current situation. “The previous government's track record over the past few years is not perfect. We are in the midst of an unprecedented energy crisis, but it is thanks to the Orbán governments' energy developments over the past 16 years and the sacrifices made by consumers that the electricity grid currently remains in operation.” He added that although they could have prioritized things differently, the current government is still solely responsible for the way the current situation is being handled. On Monday, following his meeting with the group leaders of all the parliamentary parties, the Prime Minister criticised the previous government at length for having put off relocating the pumps that supply cooling water to the Paks Nuclear Power Plant and adjusting them to lower water levels. He stressed that the Orbán governments had sixteen years to prepare the country for a situation like this, but failed to do so. “So we inherited this,” he said. Magyar announced that during the meeting with the group leaders, they had agreed to develop a water strategy. “We will allow the experts to do their job”, he said. In his view, the role of politics in this matter is simply to select the most feasible proposal from among those drafted by the experts, based on the resources available. The Prime Minister also committed to working with experts to find a short-term solution for adequately preparing the Paks NPP for a similar situation occurring again in a year or two, but also stressed that the government will work to ensure that in the long term, the country’s energy supply is much more diversified. Hungary is currently suffering from a historic drought; the water level of the Danube was minus 137 centimeters in Paks on Monday, with three units of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant already shut down. At the time of writing, the last turbine is still in operation, but its shutdown is expected within a day or two at the latest, since the low water level means that the plant’s cooling system can no longer function safely. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckg8.text: Image source, Alfred Lasteck / BBC Image caption, Boniface Mgala and a friend were pulled out of a restaurant and attacked by a mob that accused them of stealing a man's genitals By Mungai Ngige ,Â BBC Global Disinformation Unit Â and Â Alfred Lasteck ,Â BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Tunduma Published 9 hours ago More than 80 people were killed between October 2025 and July this year following false accusations about what is termed "genital theft", the BBC Global Disinformation Unit has found after gathering data from police forces across six African countries. The killings are linked to rumours that a simple tap on the shoulder can cause a man's genitals to shrink or disappear. They are being fuelled by widespread misinformation on social media. "They were shouting that we had stolen someone's genitals and we didn't have any way to escape because there was a huge crowd," Tanzanian mechanic Boniface Mgala told the BBC about his ordeal in April when he was badly beaten by those convinced he was a genital thief. His experience was similar to those in videos seen by the BBC: men claim that their genital organs - penis and testicles - have vanished or shrivelled after coming into contact with strangers and a mob then demands that alleged perpetrators return what they have supposedly stolen. Such claims are rooted in longstanding fears and superstitions - and are not new on the continent, particularly in communities where belief in witchcraft remains widespread. Social media has amplified these fears. The recent wave of rumours appears to have started last year in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where similar claims had surfaced in 2008. They progressively spread across the region to Burundi, Zambia and Tanzania as well as Mozambique, Angola, Malawi and Kenya. In Zambia, the hearsay about disappearing genitals first gained traction in March when a woman was lynched, going on to spread panic across the border in Tanzania. At his home in Mpemba near Tunduma, a busy trading town in Tanzania by the border with Zambia, Mgala traces his fingers along the sickle-shaped scar that runs down the right side of his head as he reflects on his traumatic experience. "If I had known how close I would have come to death on that day, I wouldn't have gone into that restaurant to eat. Only we don't know how close death is," the mechanic says. He and his friend had gone into Tunduma on 1 April to meet a client about a car sale and decided to eat lunch beforehand. They had not long sat down in the restaurant when they were dragged outside by a mob. Two smaller scars on his chin and a missing tooth are other visible marks of his ordeal. Amid the beating, he lost consciousness. Mgala regained awareness in hospital two days later to news that his friend had been killed. Back at his house where he lives with his wife and their four children, he now walks with a limp and says he also suffers from constant headaches. He has not been able to return to work at his mechanic shop but says neighbours and friends have helped cover the cost of some of the medicine he needs. On the same day that Mgala and his friend were attacked, commercial photographer and businessman Michael Silavwe says he witnessed another similar assault in Tunduma, where he says anxiety had been building after videos about stolen genitalia had begun circulating on TikTok. Outside his shop he saw people running and says he learned that a man had been accused nearby and was being beaten - and later set on fire. "After they set him on fire, the police arrived at the scene and everyone scattered and ran away," the 23-year-old told the BBC. In a video of the attack verified by the BBC Global Disinformation Unit and viewed more than 100,000 times across TikTok and Facebook, a group is seen beating a man while demanding he return the victim's allegedly stolen genitals. "Those incidents kept escalating and people kept getting beaten," Silavwe said, adding that at the time young people like him did feel scared, but he understands now there is no truth to the rumours. Alfred Lasteck / BBC I came to realise it was not true" Asha Steven Mwakilasa, a 50-year-old tailor and fashion designer in Tunduma, which is in Momba district, agrees: "I came to realise it was not true." This does not stop her anxiety - especially if her husband or sons are out, but she says she is grateful that the police are now mounting patrols. Momba district commissioner Elias Daniel Mwandobo told the BBC local investigations suggested there was deliberate criminal intent behind some of the incidents: "Individuals conspired to commit a crime and incite public panic for their own benefits." Another video recorded in Tanzania's main city of Dar es Salaam shows a crowd marching a man down a dusty market street, pushing, grabbing and striking him and insisting he returns the genitalia, as the man pleads his innocence. The BBC Disinformation Unit verified similar videos of attacks in Mozambique and Kenya. Dozens of these recordings of mob violence, alleged first-person accounts, warnings about alleged incidents, commentary and videos framed as reports of events in particular areas are circulating across TikTok and Facebook. Many of those analysed by the BBC, including some showing mob violence, remain online. "We are reviewing the content shared with us and will take action on those that are found to violate our policies," a Meta spokesperson told the BBC. TikTok has yet to respond to a BBC request for comment. With some social media creators, who warn viewers to be vigilant, it is often unclear whether they believe the claims or are primarily seeking engagement. Alongside these posts, some users promote so-called charms said to protect against genital theft, while comedians have parodied the claims through comedy skits. Smartphones and social media make rumours spread faster, reach larger audiences and become more difficult to control once they begin circulating, says author Julien Bonhomme. His book, The Sex Thieves: The Anthropology of a Rumor, examines how hearsay about "sex thieves" spread and why people believe them. People are not simply hearing claims that someone has lost his genitals - they are seeing distressed men say it has happened to them, or watching crowds respond to accusations, he says. Videos shared on social media can make unverified claims appear more believable, he says, because of their immediacy, describing this as "one of the most significant differences" between the current digital environment and earlier outbreaks. Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Mozambique's northern region of Cabo Delgado, where many people are displaced because of ongoing insecurity, has been badly affected by the rumours The worst-hit country has been Mozambique, where the police said in May that 55 people had been killed in six weeks, including a police officer, health workers and civil servants. Mozambique's President Daniel Chapo publicly condemned widespread rumours and deaths, saying the claims were false and the government had found no medical evidence to suggest anyone had lost a part of their body. The two healthcare workers were attacked at their home and workplace in April in Cabo Delgado province - a region that borders Tanzania which has been affected by an Islamist insurgency for nearly a decade. The health facilities in the areas of the attacks had to close for weeks while the authorities launched public awareness campaigns to counter the claims. As part of the health campaign, the government said some of the fears could be linked to Koro syndrome, a mental illness otherwise known as missing or genital retraction hysteria . The most recent incidents of violence have occurred in Kenya, where five people were killed by mobs in the coastal counties of Kwale and Mombasa. After the first incidents were reported in July, Mombasa County Commissioner Mohamed Noor blamed some content creators for spreading the claims to boost engagement "simply to attract views and attention". "Such misinformation can easily lead to loss of life," Noor told the BBC. He said police had since contained the violence and made several arrests, including a father and son who were sentenced to a year in prison after pleading guilty to assaulting a woman they accused of causing men's genitals to disappear. Similar claims also fuelled mob attacks in Malawi, leaving eight people dead. Back in Tunduma, in neighbouring Tanzania, even as mechanic Mgala recovers from the physical impact of the assault, the emotional pain is still raw. "It still hurts me deeply when I think back to the senseless manner my friend died because I still don't know what was going on," he said. "To suddenly find yourself being pelted with stones for no reason, and then end up losing your life?" https://www.wndu.com/2026/09/15/warsaw-s.text: Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WARSAW, Ind. (WNDU) - A transformational new safe haven for Michiana heroes officially opened its doors in Warsaw on September 14. Community members, veterans and local leaders gathered as The Magical Meadows Therapeutic Horseback Riding center cut the ribbon on its brand-new, 14,000-square-foot Warriors Arena. The milestone comes just two months after the center reached its $2.6 million fundraising goal in July. For years, the Warsaw-based nonprofit has provided therapeutic riding programs for children and adults with physical and cognitive disabilities. However, leadership recognized another urgent need across the region: supporting military veterans and first responders coping with trauma, post-traumatic stress, and everyday service-related stress. “We owe it to our veterans and people who fought for our great country to provide that very freedom we enjoy every day, to do everything we can to take care of them” said Kosciusko County Sheriff Jim Smith. Inside the new facility, participants in the Warriors Mount Up program can work with 25 therapy horses, learn horsemanship, ride and connect with peers walking similar paths. Organizers designed the arena with round-the-clock accessibility in mind, ensuring help is never out of reach during a mental health crisis. “They are going to have a unique key code that will allow them to be here, even if it is 2 o’clock in the morning,” said Tammy Stackhouse, founder of The Magical Meadows. “They know that if they are struggling, all they have to do is reach out — even at 3 o’clock in the morning — and we will have someone here with them.” Leaders emphasized that while equine-assisted therapy is the centerpiece, the fellowship built within the barn walls serves as a vital lifeline. “We’re celebrating. That’s the best way I can tell you,” Smith said. “It is so much more than just the horses. This is a safe space for our local heroes here in the county and our veterans in the community.” For more information on the Warriors Mount Up program or how to get involved, visit their website . Photograph: Suliane Favennec/The Guardian View image in fullscreen The man identified himself as a pianist onboard Royal Caribbean’s 14-deck cruise ship, the Ovation of the Seas. Photograph: Suliane Favennec/The Guardian California Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident Marina Dunbar Sun 8 Nov 2026 15.13 EST Last modified on Sun 8 Nov 2026 16.56 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California , fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday. The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship. Authorities believe the man may have been in the ocean for approximately nine hours before he was spotted by Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, who were returning from a fishing trip near Catalina Island. The two fishermen had spent the morning fishing for marlin when their trip took an unexpected turn. By noon, they had pulled the stranded man from the water. “I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,” Garrett told CBS News , recalling the moment the boat’s captain first saw the man in the water. The fishermen quickly worked together to bring the man onboard. Once the man regained his composure, Garrett said he identified himself as a pianist onboard Royal Caribbean’s 14-deck cruise ship, the Ovation of the Seas. According to Norton, the rescued crew member had few words to describe what he had just experienced. “The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,’” Norton said. After the rescue, the fishing crew issued an emergency maritime call, prompting Newport Beach lifeguards to respond and provide assistance. Battalion chief Adam Yacenda said the man was found approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, according to CBS, or “pretty much in the middle of the ocean”. Despite the extended time spent in the water, Norton believes unusually warm ocean temperatures may have played a significant role in the man’s survival. “You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water’s 76 degrees,” Norton said. “A different year, no way he makes it.” The circumstances surrounding the crew member’s fall from the cruise ship remain under investigation by the Coast Guard. Royal Caribbean Group acknowledged the incident and said it is assisting the employee following the ordeal. In a statement to CBS, a company spokesperson said: “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.” Explore more on these topics California West Coast Cruises news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.kyivpost.com/post/88744.text: North America Latin America Europe Eastern Europe Middle East Africa Asia Business Technology Finance Energy Agriculture Reviews EN UK Russia Europe Poland Lavrov Protests Poland’s G20 Role as US Backs Full Membership In brief: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov criticized the US on Friday, Oct. 30, for inviting Poland to participate as a full member in G20 ministerial meetings in Atlanta, claiming the unilateral invitation violated consensus rules. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Warsaw, arguing Poland’s $1 trillion economy and regional leadership justify permanent membership alongside France and Germany. by TVP World | Oct. 31, 2026, 12:08 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov speaks during a joint press conference with the Belarusian foreign minister following a joint meeting of the Boards of the Foreign Ministries of Russia and Belarus in Moscow, Nov. 25, 2025. (Photo by Alexander NEMENOV / POOL / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Friday that inviting Poland to attend G20 meetings was counterproductive and broke with the diplomatic practice of seeking consensus at such gatherings, according to Russian news agencies. “Of course, this violates the principles of diplomacy, and especially multilateral diplomacy, when members of associations such as the G20 work on the basis of consensus,” Lavrov was quoted as saying on the sidelines of a meeting of G20 foreign ministers in Atlanta. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Lavrov said Poland “contributes nothing” to the meeting. He argued that its economy was not big enough to qualify and that NATO and the EU were already well represented in the group. He added that no one had pressed Russia to accept Poland’s presence. “The Americans simply invited the Polish minister, and he came in and sat down in the chair set aside for him,” he said. Advertisement The US, which holds the rotating presidency of the G20 this year, invited Poland to take part as a full participant. It has also proposed that Poland become a full member, much like Germany or France, which are also represented through the EU. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking at a reception for the ministers at Atlanta’s Georgia Aquarium, said Poland deserved to be made a full member. “[US] President [Donald] Trump believes their economic success and growing global influence is exactly what the G20 needs to tackle the major economic challenges we all face,” Rubio said. Other Topics of Interest New Round of Ukraine Talks Set, European Representatives to Participate No date or venue has been announced for the next round of trilateral talks yet, although Witkoff confirmed it will include European partners. Economic miracle Poland’s economy passed $1 trillion for the first time last year, making it the world’s 21st largest, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The IMF expects it to grow 3.3% this year, well above the European average. Poland’s economy is already larger than those of G20 members such as Argentina and South Africa. Western officials say it could take years for Poland to be accepted as a full member given Russia’s opposition and the G20’s requirement for consensual decisions. Advertisement Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said he welcomed the push and had discussed it with a number of G20 member countries in bilateral meetings in Atlanta. He said Britain, which will head the G20 next year, had already invited Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to attend the 2027 leaders’ summit in Manchester, England, and that Poland was working to secure invitations from the following presidencies, South Korea and Mexico. He said he did not expect “enthusiasm from Russia”. Sikorski also called for a rapid ceasefire in the Black Sea that would allow safe passage for grain shipments from both Ukraine and Russia. He said Moscow must end its war against Ukraine before being allowed to resume energy sales to Europe, formerly its most lucrative market. “I spoke in favor of doing something quickly because the people of the Global South need this grain,” Sikorski told reporters. He said Ukraine must be included in any effort to end Russia’s invasion, now in its fifth year. Europe also had “cards” in the issue and should be involved, he said. Advertisement Lavrov said Russia’s position on the war was unchanged and that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s comments on maintaining strikes on Russian targets were unhelpful in preparing for new talks. “Our position is known, but what Ukraine intends to bring to the negotiating table, I don’t know,” Lavrov said. He said Zelensky’s frequent comments that Ukraine was acquiring more weapons to strike Russian targets made preparation for new talks difficult. “This kind of attitude doesn’t really help much in preparing for negotiations,” Lavrov said. Both Russia and Ukraine have said they are willing to hold further three-sided talks with the US for the first time since early in the year. Zelensky said this week that he hoped a trilateral meeting would take place in Abu Dhabi between November 6 and 10, and that Kyiv wanted Europe to be involved. On relations with Washington, Lavrov said: “Fundamental issues are not being resolved. Sanctions remain, all the sanctions from [former US President Joe] Biden are echoed by the current administration.” He pointed to a State Department announcement on Friday that it had approved the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine. Advertisement Foreign ministers at the G20 skipped the traditional group photo in Atlanta, with some making it clear they objected to appearing with Lavrov. See the original here .
